chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Lionel Hampton's early band at the Grand Terrace and Marshall Royal
summary: Jones recalls the early Hampton band with Sir Charles Thompson, Marshall Royal and Ray Perry, and Marshall's role helping Basie.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: You know, we fell in love with the Ellington outfit. In fact I think everybody was crazy about Duke, and then -- of course Basie and Lionel Hampton, I think, was one of the guys that really drew some attention at the Grand Terrace. He had quite an outfit. Sir Charles Thompson on piano, Marshall Royal, Ernie Royal, Ray Perry, the jazz violinist, and another fellow named Beckett who was quite a trombone player. You know, they had quite an outfit. Before Hamp got into his wild setup.
They were really playing some music at that point, you know.
That was when Marshall was the musical director or concert master for the band, right?
In fact Marshall has done a lot for a lot of bandleaders. He really was helpful with Basie.
I think he really ran that band beautifully, you know?
He's a very fine musician, and leader. I mean he has great leadership qualities.
